questions.prompt: What is the difference between a stored property and a computed property in Swift? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that stored properties allocate memory to save constants or variables
Explains that computed properties calculate values on demand using getters and optional setters
Mentions that computed properties do not allocate storage for values

questions.modelAnswer: In Swift, stored properties save constant or variable values in memory inside an instance. Computed properties do not store a value in memory. Instead, computed properties provide a getter and an optional setter to calculate values each time they are accessed.

questions.prompt: Why must a lazy property always be declared with var instead of let in Swift? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that lazy properties are not initialized during instance creation
States that the initial value is assigned on first access after initialization finishes
Notes that let constants require a value before initialization completes

questions.modelAnswer: A lazy property must use var because its initial value is not calculated when the instance is created. The value is calculated and assigned only on first access, after initialization finishes. Because let constants must have a value before init finishes, Swift forbids lazy let.

questions.prompt: Explain how willSet and didSet property observers work. Do they run during instance initialization? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that willSet runs right before a stored property is set and provides newValue
Explains that didSet runs right after a stored property is set and provides oldValue
States that property observers do not run when properties are set inside an initializer

questions.modelAnswer: Property observers watch when a stored property is set. willSet runs right before the new value is saved and gives you newValue. didSet runs right after the value is saved and gives you oldValue. Property observers do not run when a property gets its value inside an initializer.

questions.prompt: Why must a read-only computed property be declared with var instead of let? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that computed properties run their getter code on each read
States that let is reserved for fixed values assigned once
Mentions that the value returned by a computed property can change over time

questions.modelAnswer: A read-only computed property must use var because it runs its getter code every time you read it. Its result can change over time if the values it depends on change. Swift reserves let for fixed values stored once, so computed properties require var.

questions.prompt: How does declaring an instance as a let constant affect its var stored properties for a struct versus a class? Answer in 2–5 sentences.

rubric.criterion: Explains that for a struct (value type), a let instance freezes all properties including var properties
Explains that for a class (reference type), a let constant only locks the reference
States that var stored properties on a let class instance can still be changed

questions.modelAnswer: Because structs are value types, declaring a struct instance with let makes the whole instance immutable, so you cannot change its var properties. Classes are reference types. Declaring a class instance with let only locks which instance the reference points to, so you can still change its var stored properties.
